item.title: Roundup: Chinese mainland welcomes more discussion from Taiwan on reunification
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
Roundup: Chinese mainland welcomes more discussion from Taiwan on reunification BEIJING, Sept. 23 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese mainland welcomes more discussion in Taiwan on national reunification and is willing to conduct broad and in-depth democratic consultations with people from various sectors on the island on relations across the Taiwan Strait and the future of the Chinese nation, a mainland spokesperson said on Wednesday. Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular press conference when commenting on a recent article by a Taiwan scholar suggesting that the mainland should explore ways to end hostility and build mutual trust across the Taiwan Strait before reunification. The Taiwan question stems from China's civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China (PRC) was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war, combined with foreign interference, has kept the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Zhu said that peaceful reunification and "one country, two systems" remain the basic policy for resolving the Taiwan question and the best way to achieve national reunification. She said the Taiwan plan under a proposed "one country, two systems" framework would fully take into account Taiwan's realities, absorb opinions and suggestions from people on both sides of the Strait, and consider the interests and feelings of Taiwan compatriots. "On the common political basis of adhering to the 1992 Consensus and opposing 'Taiwan independence,' we are willing to carry out broad and in-depth democratic consultations with political parties, groups and people from all sectors in Taiwan on cross-Strait relations and the future of the Chinese nation," Zhu said. She added that the mainland welcomes suggestions from Taiwan compatriots on advancing national reunification, saying that earlier and broader discussions on reunification could create more opportunities for Taiwan's economic and social development and bring more tangible benefits to Taiwan compatriots. Her remarks came as a recent annual survey on cross-Strait relations in Taiwan showed that more than 60 percent of respondents supported continuing cross-Strait exchange platforms, expanding tourist exchanges and increasing exchanges in areas such as film, arts and sports. Zhu said the findings demonstrated that peace, development, exchanges and cooperation remain the mainstream public opinion in Taiwan and a broad consensus among different sectors in Taiwan. She said the mainland will continue to uphold the principle that people on both sides of the Strait are one family, roll out more policies and measures benefiting Taiwan compatriots, strengthen institutional support for cross-Strait integrated development, and promote personnel exchanges and cooperation in various fields. Separately, Zhu said the mainland would continue to promote cross-Strait economic exchanges and cooperation so that people on both sides of the Strait can share the benefits of peaceful and integrated development of cross-Strait relations. She noted that relevant parties on both sides have been working to implement 10 policy measures announced by the mainland in April to promote cross-Strait exchanges and cooperation, helping more Taiwan farmers and fishermen expand into the mainland market. According to Zhu, multiple Taiwan packaging plants, orchards and food enterprises have been registered on the mainland, while customs clearance efficiency has improved and logistics have become more convenient. On transportation links, Zhu said direct cross-Strait passenger air services have yet to fully return to normal due to obstruction and interference by the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities. From January to August this year, 4.22 million passenger trips were made on direct cross-Strait flights, up 12.9 percent year on year, reflecting strong market demand and a strong desire for exchanges among people on both sides of the Strait, Zhu said. She called on the Taiwan side to remove unreasonable restrictions on cross-Strait air transportation and allow airlines on both sides to arrange flights based on market demand. Commenting on the annual Shanghai-Taipei City Forum, Zhu described it as an important platform for city-to-city exchanges across the Strait and said both cities had remained in communication over arrangements for this year's event. The forum, which has been held for 16 consecutive years, has developed well-established practices and is expected to proceed as scheduled this year, she said. In response to recent remarks by Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te on increasing Taiwan's "defense spending" to "safeguard peace through strength," Zhu reiterated the mainland's position that there is only one China in the world and Taiwan is part of China. She said the DPP authorities' stubborn pursuit of "Taiwan independence," deliberate escalation of confrontation across the Taiwan Strait, and attempts to seek "Taiwan independence" through military means and external support make them the chief culprit in undermining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait. No matter how much is spent on military budgets or weapons purchases, Zhu said, it cannot change the historical trend toward national reunification.

item.title: Increased 'defense' spending won't prevent inevitable failure, mainland spokeswoman warns
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
Increased 'defense' spending won't prevent inevitable failure, mainland spokeswoman warns A Chinese mainland spokeswoman on Wednesday warned Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party authorities that no amount of increased "defense spending" or weapons purchases could change the inevitable failure of "Taiwan independence". Zhu Fenglian, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made these remarks at a regular news conference in response to Taiwan leader Lai Ching-te's recent claim that Taiwan's "defense" budget will reach 5 percent of its GDP by 2030. Zhu accused Lai's administration of stubbornly adhering to a separatist stance by pursuing "Taiwan independence" and advancing this agenda through force and reliance on external forces, thereby deliberately escalating tensions and confrontations across the Taiwan Strait. She described the DPP authorities as the culprits responsible for undermining peace and stability and disrupting the status quo in the Taiwan Strait. "There is only one China in the world, and Taiwan is part of China," Zhu stated, emphasizing that this is the actual status quo in the Taiwan Strait. Lai recently claimed that his responsibility is to ensure Taiwan is better prepared and more capable of maintaining the status quo and preventing peace from being undermined by unilateral provocations "in the face of profound changes in the international situation and the continued escalation of the threat posed by the mainland". In response, Zhu criticized Lai's administration for advocating increased "defense" spending for their own political interests while using public funds to expand military capabilities. "This runs counter to the mainstream public opinion in Taiwan and will only push Taiwan into greater danger," she warned, asserting that no matter how much they increase their budgets or how many weapons they purchase, they cannot alter the inevitable failure of "Taiwan independence" or halt the trend toward national reunification.

item.title: Mainland criticizes Taiwan's DPP for donating vessel to Philippines
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
Mainland criticizes Taiwan's DPP for donating vessel to Philippines A Chinese mainland spokeswoman on Wednesday criticized the Democratic Progressive Party authorities in Taiwan for donating a decommissioned "coast guard" vessel to the Philippines for use as a law enforcement vessel, accusing them of abandoning the national position. Stressing that Taiwan is part of China, Zhu Fenglian, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said that the two sides across the Taiwan Strait should jointly safeguard the country's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, as well as the overall and fundamental interests of the Chinese nation. According to reports, a decommissioned 500-ton patrol vessel of Taiwan's "coast guard" was found to have been transferred to the Philippines for use as a law enforcement vessel. Zhu noted that the DPP authorities have turned a blind eye to the launch of talks between Japan and the Philippines on the delimitation of maritime boundaries in waters east of Taiwan. "Rather than doing their utmost to protect the interests of people on the island, they have instead assisted such actions, increasing the risk of harm to the rights and interests of Taiwan's fishermen and abandoning their national position, which is deeply regrettable," she said. Meanwhile, Lin Chia-lung, head of the island's external affairs department, recently announced that Taiwan is preparing to open a representative office in Cebu, the Philippines. The move has also sparked controversy on the island, as it came amid the so-called delimitation talks between Japan and the Philippines. In response, Zhu said the DPP authorities' stubborn pursuit of "Taiwan independence" by relying on external forces cannot change the fact that Taiwan is part of China, nor can it shake the broad consensus and fundamental framework of the international community upholding the one-China principle. "Such efforts will only end in failure," she added. She also urged the Philippines to adhere to the one-China principle and stop sending wrong signals to separatist forces seeking "Taiwan independence".

item.title: Taiwan's Kuma Academy criticized for promoting separatism and wartime atmosphere
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
Taiwan's Kuma Academy criticized for promoting separatism and wartime atmosphere The Chinese mainland on Wednesday criticized the Kuma Academy in Taiwan for stoking a wartime atmosphere and engaging in separatist activities under the guise of making a profit, calling the organization a "Taiwan independence profiteer". Zhu Fenglian, a spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said the academy's misconduct was deplorable and warned that separatist activities in pursuit of "Taiwan independence" would be met with punishment. The Kuma Academy recently called on cities and counties across Taiwan to incorporate "wartime disaster preparedness" into local disaster-prevention planning and advocated building a more comprehensive whole-of-society "defense" system on the island. "The remarks are completely misguided and amount to promoting the idea of turning Taiwan into a battlefield, which will inevitably face opposition from the people of Taiwan," Zhu said. She stated that the Kuma Academy had gone to great lengths to stoke a wartime atmosphere and cultivate a "seed of violence" in Taiwan society while openly engaging in separatist activities, making it a de facto base for "Taiwan independence". Zhu added that the organization uses the guise of lectures, training programs, and outdoor exercises to profit from its activities and colludes with external forces to defraud people of their money, making it a "Taiwan independence profiteer".

item.title: The Taiwan Affairs Office of Guangxi Conducts Visits, Services and Policy Briefings in Yulin: Practical Policies and Heartwarming Services Boost Confidence among Taiwan Compatriots
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-18
The Taiwan Affairs Office of Guangxi Conducts Visits, Services and Policy Briefings in Yulin: Practical Policies and Heartwarming Services Boost Confidence among Taiwan Compatriots Source: Taiwan.cnUpdated: 2026-09-18
Sep 18(Taiwan.cn)—Recently, the Taiwan Affairs Office of Guangxi held a policy briefing in Yulin City to explain the Party's policies, laws and regulations concerning Taiwan, as well as preferential policies and measures benefiting Taiwan compatriots. Around 100 participants attended the event, including representatives of Taiwan-invested enterprises and Taiwan businesspeople residing in Yulin, mainland spouses of Taiwanese nationals, relatives of Taiwan compatriots, Taiwan teachers working in Yulin, and officials from relevant municipal departments. The briefing addressed issues of greatest concern to Taiwan compatriots. Legal experts systematically reviewed laws and regulations related to Taiwan affairs and provided in-depth explanations supported by practical cases involving Guangxi's preferential policies for Taiwan compatriots. Officials from the Yulin Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau elaborated on policies covering employment, entrepreneurship, talent introduction and social security support for Taiwan compatriots. Staff from the Yulin Municipal Tax Service explained preferential tax policies for Taiwan-invested enterprises item by item. The informative and pragmatic briefing was praised by participating Taiwan compatriots as "highly informative." Following the briefing, Taiwan compatriot attendees visited the Guangxi headquarters of Want Want Group, the R&D headquarters of Fuchang Group and the Yulin Association of Taiwan-invested Enterprises. They gained first-hand insights into the operations and development of key Taiwan-invested enterprises by visiting their production sites. During exchanges, participants stated that they would remain confident in development, seize opportunities and continue to expand their investments in Yulin. (Jointly reported by Taiwan.cn and the Taiwan Affairs Office of Yulin Guangxi) Related Stories

item.title: The Taiwan Affairs Office of Tieling Visits Taiwan Compatriots Affected by Flood Disaster
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-18
The Taiwan Affairs Office of Tieling Visits Taiwan Compatriots Affected by Flood Disaster Source: Taiwan.cnUpdated: 2026-09-18
Sep 18(Taiwan.cn)—On September 16, Li Jian, Member of the Standing Committee of the CPC Tieling Municipal Committee and Director of the United Front Work Department, led a team to visit Mr. Zhu and his wife, Taiwan compatriots residing in Tieling. The team held discussions with them to learn about their production and living conditions, conveying the care and warmth of the Party committee and government. On July 13 this year, Tieling was hit by short-duration heavy rainfall, triggering floods in some areas. Mr. Zhu and his wife, who had returned for a family visit at that time, were trapped. Local authorities activated emergency responses immediately and carried out prompt rescue operations to fully safeguard the lives and property of the Taiwan compatriots. After the flood crisis, the Taiwan Affairs Office of Tieling continued to follow up on their situation, monitoring their health and daily life, and providing consistent follow-up services, allowing the Taiwan compatriots to truly feel the care of the local community. During this trip back to Tieling, Mr. Zhu and his wife came specifically to express gratitude for the timely rescue provided by the local government and fire rescue teams during the flood. During the meeting, Li Jian inquired in detail about their post-disaster physical recovery and their itinerary for this visit to Tieling. He stated that compatriots across the Taiwan Strait share the same bloodline and are closely bonded as family. Offering assistance in times of crisis is the inescapable duty of local functional departments. Whenever Taiwan compatriots return to Tieling, the CPC Tieling Municipal Committee and Tieling Municipal Government will provide thoughtful and dedicated services, act as trusted friends for Taiwan compatriots, and earnestly implement various preferential policies benefiting Taiwan compatriots, so that they can live in Tieling with peace of mind. Mr. Zhu and his wife said with emotion that the timely rescue amid the crisis made them deeply experience family-like warmth and witness the spirit of "compatriots on both sides of the Strait are one family." They found it hard to let go of the kindness and sincere concern in Tieling. They expressed their willingness to share their personal experiences in Tieling with relatives and friends in Taiwan, introduce the real economic and social development of Liaoning Province, encourage more Taiwan compatriots to visit Tieling, and help deepen cross-strait people-to-people exchanges. item.title: Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-02-11
BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday denounced Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te for ignoring the heinous crimes committed by Japan during its colonial rule over Taiwan, describing their flattering remarks toward Japan as utterly disgraceful. Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks in response to a media inquiry about Lai's intention to work with Japan to "deal with regional challenges." Zhu also urged the Japanese side to retract Sanae Takaichi's erroneous remarks on Taiwan, handle Taiwan-related issues prudently, and abide by the one-China principle with concrete actions. item.title: Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson has condemned Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for imposing restrictions and obstacles on cross-Strait exchanges in pursuit of their "Taiwan independence" agenda and selfish gains. The DPP authorities, led by Lai Ching-te, are the biggest obstacle to cross-Strait interactions and their acts have drawn strong criticism from various sectors in Taiwan, Zhu Fenglian, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a regular press briefing on Wednesday. Zhu expressed the hope that Taiwan compatriots will firmly oppose the retrogressive actions of the DPP authorities and promote exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait in various fields. She noted that cross-Strait flight routes have been disrupted due to interference from the DPP authorities, with previously operated destinations yet to resume normal operations. In 2025, the average passenger load factor on cross-Strait routes reached 80 percent, reflecting the strong need for direct flights between the two sides of the Strait, Zhu said. "We hope that the Taiwan side will heed public opinion and lift unreasonable restrictions on cross-Strait air transport as soon as possible," she added.

item.title: Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for hyping up security risks of mainland apps
item.description:
Published: 2026-01-29
Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for hyping up security risks of mainland apps Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-01-29
BEIJING, Jan. 28 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday criticized Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for hyping up the so-called information security risks of applications from the mainland. Zhang Han, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, stated at a press conference that the DPP moves have deprived people in Taiwan, especially the youth, of their right to know and the freedom to use social networking platforms. Noting that such moves reveal the fear and insecurity of the DPP authorities, Zhang said they will have to face the dire consequences of their wayward actions.
